Name: Tomisine R Bazzell
Badge: Teacher as Researcher | Sustaining Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

Looking back, I learned that I am very good at scaffolding and modeling for my students, but this is more about them and them connecting to reading. I love how this layering strategy gives the students ownership and connections that I can't make for them. I have decided that it is so good for students to take ownership of their writing that I will be doing this more often. I still need to build writing stamina for the students and will start of the year with a writing journal next year.

Think back to a moment during the lesson sequence that stands out. It could be a comment from a student, an unexpected challenge or success, a shift in engagement, or a moment when your own thinking changed. Describe what happened and why this moment feels meaningful to you now. What does it reveal:
The main moment I remember is when my student reading at a 1st grade reading level said, "I wonder if my grandpa knew there was AI when he was younger" and I told him he can ask. That is when I really realized when they do the work, they make better connections to their lives.
As you look over the drafts your students produced in this lesson sequence, what early patterns, surprises, or questions are emerging for you? What aspects of your students’ writing are you most curious to explore more deeply with colleagues during our April regroup? What, if any, questions do you h:
I noticed that many of them need help expanding on the topic. However, for the grade levels they perform at, I was very impressed. I explored how to get students writing more and setting up daily routines for stamina at the re-group.
